name: The Linden of King Matthias

location.address: Bojnice Castle park (Zámocký park), near the castle approach, Bojnice

verified_sources: https://www.teraz.sk/regiony/bojnice-zamok-park-lipa-kral-matej/139335-clanok.html (TASR news, 2015, quoting the castle museum director)
access: Free; stands in the public castle park near the approach to Bojnice Castle (the castle building and zoo require separate paid tickets, the park itself does not). The tree is fenced off and visitors may not approach the trunk, a restriction put in place as part of its ongoing conservation since the 1950s; it can be viewed but not touched.
transport: In the town of Bojnice; short walk from the Bojnice bus/rail stops to the castle park entrance
verify_notes:
CONTAINER DECISION: new single-tree place, proposed id prefix 'boj', place name 'Bojnice' (the castle park). Passes the 2026-08-31 single-famous-tree exception: this is the single most-documented, highest-demand candidate in the whole leads batch (Slovak AND English Wikipedia articles exist, 'Linden Tree of King Matthias'; ~195 reads/month per the brief), it sits inside one of Slovakia's most-visited tourist sites (Bojnice Castle), and it is repeatedly called probably the oldest tree in Slovakia. People visit Bojnice Castle already in large numbers; the tree is a genuine, independently named reason to look for something specific once there, not a generic park tree. Not folding into Bratislava (different city/region entirely, ~170km away).

ALIVE: confirmed alive as of the most recent locatable reporting (WebSearch summary of 2024/2025 Slovak coverage: 'lipa je pod dohľadom a vďaka pravidelným konzíliám je lipa v dobrom stave', i.e. under expert annual review and in good condition). It nearly died in the early 1950s (severe dieback, small yellow-green leaves, weak flowering per the official castle site's own conservation account) and was saved by a 1952-53 restoration (dead wood and cavity clay removed, fungicide treatment, cavities sealed, wooden supports); a 2015 TASR piece quotes the museum director confirming continued flowering and root/irrigation work since the 1990s. So this is a veteran tree that came close to dying and has been actively kept alive for 70+ years, which is itself the story.

AGE: legend says planted 1301 by Matus Cak Trenciansky; official castle site, both Wikipedias and every tourism source repeat 'over 700 years' as an inherited figure rather than a fresh dendrological reading (the Slovak Wikipedia page itself notes current methods cannot establish the tree's true age). I found (but could NOT fetch past a 402 paywall after two attempts) a regional SME/MY Hornà Nitra piece whose own headline translates roughly to 'it never witnessed royal diets and its age has been exaggerated by legend, what we actually know is mostly fiction' -- flagging this explicitly rather than silently repeating '700 years' as settled fact. Following the brief's rule (repeat a vague age from a real source as vaguely as given, never sharpen it), age_estimate is left as the repeated tradition figure with no numeric age_min/age_max, since no source gives a derived figure I can defend; the writer should say plainly this is legend, disputed by at least one regional news piece, not a measured age.

MEASUREMENTS: official castle site gives trunk circumference (kmen) 11m = girth_cm 1100 (recorded), height 9m today (down from a historic 28m before major limb loss), crown diameter 5m today (down from a historic ~36m). Circumference at the very base (pri pni) given separately as 12.5m -- noted as a base/buttress measurement, not the trunk girth, so the writer should not conflate the two.

ACCESS: multiple sources place the tree in the castle's own park, one describing it as standing 'in front of the castle entrance' (pred vstupom do zamku), which reads as the approach area rather than inside the ticketed courtyard/zoo. I could not fully settle from open sources whether the park itself ever charges separate admission from the castle building and zoo (both of which do); the balance of sources describes the park as a walkable public space with no ticket mentioned for the park itself. A 2015 news piece confirms the immediate vicinity of the tree has been fenced off to visitors since restoration work began, i.e. viewable, not approachable, which is recorded honestly in access rather than treated as a full block.

LOCATION: coordinates taken from the Commons category lead (48.780833, 18.577323), presumably geotagged from photographs taken at the tree; I have not independently verified this pin against a park map, so marked approximate rather than confirmed. A note for the writer/reader: a 'daughter' linden, genetically propagated from this tree, was planted nearby in 2005 and by 2015 was nearly as tall as the mother tree; it is not itself an ancient tree and is not recorded as a separate entry, but is good color for the story.

DUPLICATES: this lead appears twice in data/leads/_famous-slovakia.json under the identical name and coordinates; treated as one tree.

name: The Linden at U Belanských

location.address: U Belanských settlement, Turá Lúka (part of Myjava), beside a side street near house no. 564

verified_sources: https://www.krizom-krazom.online/lipa-u-belanskych/ (independent Slovak protected-trees resource, with its own GPS reading)
access: Free; stands beside a side street in the residential U Belanských settlement of Turá Lúka, on the edge of two land parcels. No gate or fee mentioned by either source, and its coordinates from krizom-krazom.eu (48.72716, 17.52227) sit within metres of this lead's own pin, consistent with a roadside tree rather than one set back on private ground.
transport: In the Turá Lúka district on the western edge of Myjava town; nearest access is by local road, no rail station in Myjava itself
verify_notes: CONTAINER DECISION: new single-tree place, proposed id prefix 'myj', place name 'Myjava' (Turá Lúka district). Myjava is roughly 90km from Bratislava, far outside any day-trip boundary, so this cannot join Bratislava. Passes the single-famous-tree exception: independently described as probably the thickest tree in Slovakia (girth 1015cm, measured at 130cm height), one of its oldest at ~620 years, carries a genuine local-history story (partisans reportedly hid inside its hollow trunk during WWII), and placed 3rd nationally in Ekopolis's 2009 Tree of the Year competition (won 333 EUR for its own upkeep). This is more than a fine local specimen: it is a named, competition-recognised tree that the town itself promotes as a destination on its own tourism page. TWO SOURCES: the official Myjava municipal tourism page and krizom-krazom.eu (an independent Slovak protected-trees documentation resource) agree on species, ~620 years, 16m height, 1015cm girth (measured at 130cm) and the WWII partisan story. They differ by a few years on the protection/designation date (myjava.sk says declared a protected natural monument in 1990 with a 2002 care programme; krizom-krazom.eu says 1996), a minor register-date discrepancy rather than a factual conflict, noted for the writer rather than resolved. ALIVE: both sources describe it in the present tense as a standing, protected, actively cared-for tree (the 2002 conservation programme, the 2009 prize money earmarked for its maintenance); no report of decline or death found. MEASUREMENTS: girth_cm 1015, explicitly measured at 130cm (breast height), both sources agree; crown diameter given as 11m by myjava.sk. LOCATION: krizom-krazom.eu gives GPS 48 43'37.787"N 17 31'20.172"E, which converts to 48.72716, 17.52227, essentially identical to this lead's own coordinate (48.727113, 17.522182), so marked confirmed rather than approximate. Both sources place it on a side street/parcel boundary in a residential settlement, not inside a private garden. DUPLICATES: none found for this name in the leads file.

name: The Grinava Poplar

location.address: Limbašská cesta, near the former Strapák's Mill, Grinava district of Pezinok

verified_sources: data/registers/slovakia-chranene-stromy.json (register_id 499, Štátna ochrana prírody SR, CC BY 4.0, publishable: true)
access: Free, standing beside a public road (Limbašská cesta) near a former mill; no gate or private-land indication in either source
transport: Pezinok zastávka, a railway stop on the Bratislava-Zilina line inside the Grinava district itself (closer to Bratislava than Pezinok's main station), roughly 15 minutes by train from Bratislava hlavná stanica, then a short walk to Limbašská cesta; exact walk time from the stop to this tree not established
verify_notes:
CONTAINER DECISION: joins Bratislava as a day-trip tree (next free id brt_007), labeled honestly as Grinava/Pezinok rather than Bratislava proper. Straight-line distance from Bratislava centre is ~18km, but the deciding fact is the direct rail stop: 'Pezinok zastavka' (until the late 1970s named plainly 'Grinava') sits on the Bratislava-Zilina line between Bratislava-Raca and the main Pezinok station, i.e. inside Grinava itself, and the Bratislava-Pezinok run overall is 17-21 minutes by train, so a stop before the main station is comfortably within the ~30-minute public-transport day-trip boundary. This is our OWN register tree (register_id 499, publishable: true, CC BY 4.0), so licence and reuse are already cleared; krizom-krazom.eu is the second independent source and the two agree on species (topol cierny / black poplar), ~40m height, 705cm girth, 19m crown, coordinates (48.2805, 17.2408 vs the register's own 48.2805/17.2408, essentially identical) and the Limbasska cesta / Strapak's mill locality.

ALIVE: a Wiki Loves Earth 2023 photograph (File:499, Grinavsky topol - pohlad z juhozapadu.jpg, taken 2023-07-30, CC BY-SA 4.0, photographer TomphanTK) shows the tree standing and in leaf as of summer 2023, the most recent dated evidence found.

AGE: krizom-krazom.eu states '100 years' as a flat figure with no stated reference year, so I have not derived a band from it (the register's protection year of 2007 could push today's age closer to 115-120 if that was the measurement year, but that is my own arithmetic on an unstated premise, not a sourced figure, so age_min/age_max are left empty rather than invented). The writer should present this as an approximate, source-stated figure rather than a precise one.

MEASUREMENTS: girth_cm 705 (agreed by both sources); height given as 40m by krizom-krazom and 36.9m by a separate secondary mention found in search, both clearly the same tree, noted as a minor measurement discrepancy rather than resolved.

PHOTO CANDIDATE: File:499,_Grinavsky_topol_-_pohlad_z_juhozapadu.jpg viewed via description/metadata (not full-resolution pixel inspection): CC BY-SA 4.0, TomphanTK, taken 2023-07-30 in daylight, described as a southwest-angle view of the poplar. Could not fully confirm framing (tree fills most of frame vs distant view) from the fetch tool used, so leaving photo status to a dedicated photo-judge pass rather than approving it myself; flagged here as the strongest candidate of the three filenames on this lead (the other two are 'pohlad z vychodu 1' and 'pohlad z vychodu 2', same photographer/session).
